result.topic_en: This is the opening page of Euler's paper on very large prime numbers, where he compares finding the law of the primes to squaring the circle and argues that a method achieving either would be very useful.
result.transcription:

DE
NVMERIS PRIMIS
VALDE MAGNIS.
Auctore
L. EVLERO.

Vix vllus reperietur Geometra, qui non, ordinem
numerorum primorum inueſtigando, haud parum
temporis inutiliter conſumſerit: videtur enim
lex, qua numeri primi progrediuntur, in Arithmetica
aeque abſtruſae eſſe indaginis, atque in Geometria cir-
culi quadratura: ac ſi huius indagatio pro deſperata eſt
habenda, non leuiores adſunt rationes, quae et ordinis,
quo numeri primi ſe inuicem ſequuntur, cognitionem
nos in perpetuum fugere perſuadent. Cum deinde
etiam circuli quadratura, quamuis innoteſceret, vix
quicquam vtilitatis allatura perhibeatur, eodem iure ne-
gare licebit, ex ordine numerorum primorum perſpecto
vllum vſum eſſe redundaturum. Verum tamen nemo
facile dubitabit, quin methodus ipſa, quae nos vel ad
circuli quadraturam, vel ad legem progreſſionis nume-
rorum primorum manuduceret, quoniam hae res tam
diu fruſtra ſunt anquiſitae, eximium vſum ſit praeſta-
tura, propterea quod maxima impedimenta, quibus hae
inueſtigationes adhuc fuerunt implicatae, feliciter ſupe-
rauerit; ita vt inde omni iure ſumma ſubſidia per
totam Matheſin nobis polliceri poſſemus. Haec ideo

items.quote:
videtur enim
lex, qua numeri primi progrediuntur, in Arithmetica
aeque abſtruſae eſſe indaginis, atque in Geometria cir-
culi quadratura
items.english: For the law by which the prime numbers proceed seems to be as obscure a subject of inquiry in arithmetic as the quadrature of the circle is in geometry.

items.quote:
non leuiores adſunt rationes, quae et ordinis,
quo numeri primi ſe inuicem ſequuntur, cognitionem
nos in perpetuum fugere perſuadent
items.english: There are no less weighty reasons which persuade us that knowledge of the order in which the prime numbers follow one another will escape us forever.

items.quote:
eodem iure ne-
gare licebit, ex ordine numerorum primorum perſpecto
vllum vſum eſſe redundaturum
items.english: With the same right one may deny that any use would result from having perceived the order of the prime numbers.

items.quote:
nemo
facile dubitabit, quin methodus ipſa, quae nos vel ad
circuli quadraturam, vel ad legem progreſſionis nume-
rorum primorum manuduceret, quoniam hae res tam
diu fruſtra ſunt anquiſitae, eximium vſum ſit praeſta-
tura
items.english: No one will easily doubt that the method itself which would lead us either to the quadrature of the circle or to the law of progression of the prime numbers, since these things have been sought in vain for so long, would be of outstanding use.
